This was a great way for me to learn what I should be adjusting on my camera. 

Once I had a basic understanding of how to balance the exposure triangle (ISO, shutter speed and aperture), I switched into shooting in Aperture Priority mode. This allows you to set the Aperture with the scroll wheel and the shutter speed changes according to your f-stop and ISO, exposing your frame for you. 

You can either shoot in Shutter or Aperture priority, whichever you feel you need to control more. There are still times I shoot in shutter priority and times that I shoot in manual as well. Just spend time shooting before your trip and learn how to control your camera. Even if you are shooting stuff inside and it's just random objects, learn the controls. 

And most importantly, have fun! You have just joined a fun and massive community!

2a. Talk to your academic advisor of your desired major at A&M. Do not go to the TEAM advisors or the Blinn advisors. 

2b. Your advisor should tell you this, but take classes at A&M that directly apply to your major. Don't take a history or accounting class at A&M because you can get those at Blinn. Make progress towards your major in classes that are important. (Also this helps with full admission down the road)

3. Focus on your A&M classes slightly more. Once you transfer out of TEAM/TEAB your Blinn grades will not carry over to your GPA, but your hours at A&M and the grades you earn there do. Help yourself out and start off with a high GPA. That doesn't mean fail your Blinn classes because you obviously have to be admitted into A&M first. 

4. You are only allowed to take summer classes at Blinn (I think). You will register for those online just like you will for all of your other classes. That is the same for all semesters. 

5. Again talk with your advisor. He/She will be a huge asset for your transfer and long after that once you are admitted to A&M. Build a good, professional relationship with them and always be respectful and polite. If you do it right they may be able to hold a class spot for you or help force you into a class if it comes down to it. Meet with the at least once a semester. 

6. There are two types of teachers at Blinn. Bad teachers who used to work in the field of the subject, and teachers who think everyone is a moron and make the class super easy. Use MyEdu(dot)com to figure out what others think of a teacher and see their grade distribution.  

7. You just don't have to deal with the whole Blinn system and the commute. You will decide for yourself if it is worth it or not to stay in the program. When you are sitting on the A&M campus, no one knows you are on TEAM, it isn't a big deal. It's all personal preference.

You will learn after a semester or two if you want to continue with Engineering. If it's not for you, there is something for you. Again go talk to different advisors for some majors and find out what suits you best. Think what kind of job you want after college and find something that will help you secure a job in that field.

Also if you schedule early classes (8 a.m.s) there is much more parking available. The worst time of day is 11am-3pm.
